:::{#thm-mvn-conditional}
#### The conditional distribution of a block of a multivariate normal vector

Let $\vX \sim \Normal_p\paren{\vecf{\mean}, \matr{\covmat}}$ (@def-mvn),
cut into $\vX = \begin{bmatrix} \vX_1 \\ \vX_2 \end{bmatrix}$
with $k$ and $m$ components,
and cut $\vecf{\mean}$ and $\matr{\covmat}$ to match:

$$
\vecf{\mean} = \begin{bmatrix} \vecf{\mean}_1 \\ \vecf{\mean}_2 \end{bmatrix},
\quad
\matr{\covmat}
= \begin{bmatrix}
\matr{\covmat}_{11} & \matr{\covmat}_{12} \\
\matr{\covmat}_{21} & \matr{\covmat}_{22}
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Let $\matr{S} = \matr{\covmat}_{22} - \matr{\covmat}_{21}\matr{\covmat}_{11}^{-1}\matr{\covmat}_{12}$.
Then, given $\vX_1 = \vx_1$,

$$
\vX_2 \mid \vX_1 = \vx_1
\sim \Normal_m\paren{
\vecf{\mean}_2 + \matr{\covmat}_{21}\matr{\covmat}_{11}^{-1}(\vx_1 - \vecf{\mean}_1),
\matr{S}}.
$$

:::

::: proof

[$\matr{\covmat}$ is positive definite](#def-mvn),
so by the
[block inverse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-diagonalization.html#thm-block-inverse)
theorem,
$\matr{S}$ is positive definite,
and $\matr{\covmat}^{-1}$ has blocks $\matr{\Omega}_{ij}$ with

$$
\matr{\Omega}_{22} = \matr{S}^{-1},
\quad
\matr{\Omega}_{21} = -\matr{S}^{-1}\matr{\covmat}_{21}\matr{\covmat}_{11}^{-1}.
$$

Write $\vecf{d}_1 = \vx_1 - \vecf{\mean}_1$ and $\vecf{d}_2 = \vx_2 - \vecf{\mean}_2$.
The conditional density of $\vX_2$ given $\vX_1 = \vx_1$ is the joint density divided by the marginal density of $\vx_1$,
and the marginal density does not depend on $\vx_2$.
So as a function of $\vx_2$, the conditional density is proportional to the joint density,
which is proportional to the exponential of

$$
\ba
-\frac{1}{2}\paren{
\tp{\vecf{d}_1}\matr{\Omega}_{11}\vecf{d}_1
+ 2\tp{\vecf{d}_2}\matr{\Omega}_{21}\vecf{d}_1
+ \tp{\vecf{d}_2}\matr{\Omega}_{22}\vecf{d}_2}.
\ea
$$

The first term does not involve $\vx_2$,
so it goes into the constant of proportionality.
Substituting $\matr{\Omega}_{21}$ and $\matr{\Omega}_{22}$ into the other two terms:

$$
\ba
2\tp{\vecf{d}_2}\matr{\Omega}_{21}\vecf{d}_1
+ \tp{\vecf{d}_2}\matr{\Omega}_{22}\vecf{d}_2
&= \tp{\vecf{d}_2}\matr{S}^{-1}\vecf{d}_2
- 2\tp{\vecf{d}_2}\matr{S}^{-1}\matr{\covmat}_{21}\matr{\covmat}_{11}^{-1}\vecf{d}_1
&& \text{(substitute)} \\
&= \tp{\paren{\vecf{d}_2 - \vecf{c}}}\matr{S}^{-1}\paren{\vecf{d}_2 - \vecf{c}}
- \tp{\vecf{c}}\matr{S}^{-1}\vecf{c}
&& \text{(complete the square, with } \vecf{c} = \matr{\covmat}_{21}\matr{\covmat}_{11}^{-1}\vecf{d}_1 \text{)}
\ea
$$

The last term does not involve $\vx_2$ either.
Since $\vecf{d}_2 - \vecf{c} = \vx_2 - \paren{\vecf{\mean}_2 + \vecf{c}}$,
the conditional density of $\vX_2$ is proportional to

$$
\ef{-\frac{1}{2}
\tp{\paren{\vx_2 - \paren{\vecf{\mean}_2 + \vecf{c}}}}
\matr{S}^{-1}
\paren{\vx_2 - \paren{\vecf{\mean}_2 + \vecf{c}}}},
$$

which is proportional to the $\Normal_m\paren{\vecf{\mean}_2 + \vecf{c}, \matr{S}}$ density.
A conditional density integrates to 1,
so the constant of proportionality is the one that makes this the $\Normal_m\paren{\vecf{\mean}_2 + \vecf{c}, \matr{S}}$ density.

:::
